title: Additive M5 symmetry-protected isolated-node candidate contract
question: Can the required structurally distinct isolated-node alternative be specified as a finite conservative candidate with an explicit symmetry and observable map, while preserving the established T-054 and T-059 methods?
method: Freeze a finite periodic three-dimensional lattice, a four-component complex field, canonical momenta, a Wilson-regularized chiral symbol, and the m=0 node convention in one additive candidate manifest.

State the exact Clifford, chiral, isolated-node, coercive Hamiltonian, and finite-flow obligations separately so a future primary, independent, hostile, and Lean audit cannot silently promote a design equation.
Define F_reg node, dispersion, density, chiral, current, and two-time observables, while leaving F_lim, F_eff, F_obs, uncertainty, and prospective holdout stages explicitly missing.
Keep the existing T-054 forward tournament, T-059 observation-first inverse lane, owner order, finite/uniform/physical layer firewall, and stopped-loop registry unchanged.
finding: A second, structurally distinct candidate can be recorded without changing the research method: a finite Wilson-regularized chiral lattice symbol with m=0 has an explicit isolated-node target at the origin of the declared momentum grid, and a positive sextic Hamiltonian supplies a conservative finite dynamics contract. The statement is only a design contract. Clifford identities, node uniqueness, symmetry protection, flow conservation, all limit stages, candidate comparison, and observation mapping remain unverified admission obligations.
decision_reason: The frozen Round-1 triage requires an isolated-node alternative in addition to the compact-gauge M3 design. This manifest satisfies that inventory requirement additively, makes the symmetry and node tests falsifiable, and preserves the established methods and promotion firewalls. It does not select or repair an existing candidate and does not convert a finite node into a physical QFT claim.
decision_scope: T0 Pre-A candidate-design scope only. The finite symbol, Hamiltonian, and observable list are proposed inputs; no theorem, numerical result, physical model, candidate score, or holdout credit is admitted.
assumptions: The finite lattice, momentum representatives, matrix relations, m=0 pinning, and Hamiltonian normalization are exactly those in the manifest.
The node statement is tested only on the declared finite momentum grid before any continuum interpretation.
The future proof owner treats chiral protection as a restricted symmetry-preserving perturbation test, not as a generic stability assertion.
Any statistical or quantum realization is versioned separately and cannot be inferred from this classical finite contract.
missing_assumptions: An authorized source owner and independently hash-pinned implementation of the Clifford matrices, symbol, Hamiltonian, and flow.
Primary, non-importing independent, hostile, and Lean checks of the Clifford algebra, isolated-node iff statement, chiral symmetry, coercivity, and energy conservation.
A declared state or ensemble, quantum representation if used, and complete uncertainty, covariance, and nuisance law.
Uniform regulator, volume, interaction, and node-stability estimates with a declared limit order and counterterm policy.
A complete F_lim/F_eff/F_obs map and a prospective holdout separated from discovery and calibration data.
A common discriminator comparison against M0, M1, M2, PA-M3-COMPACT-U1-HAMILTONIAN-v0, and PA-M5-NL3-SV-v0.
